question: Directive (EU) 2019/904 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment was transposed into Italian law by way of Legislative Decree No 196/21, and Article 5(3) of that Decree exempts, in certain cases, from the prohibition on the placing on the market of single-use products, those made of ‘biodegradable and compostable’ material certified in accordance with European standard UNI EN 13432 or UNI EN 14995.
This would seem to conflict with the provisions of the Directive itself. Can the Commission therefore answer the following questions: 1.
Has it taken action, or does it plan to take action, against this exemption of ‘biodegradable and compostable’ plastics provided for in Legislative Decree No 196/21?
If so, what action has it taken?
answer: The Single-Use Plastics Directive (SUPD) (1) specifies in Recital 11 that the definition of plastics covers biodegradable plastics. Compostable plastics is a subset of biodegradable plastics (2). Therefore, the prohibition under Article 5 of the SUPD applies to the placing on the market of certain single-use products made of biodegradable and compostable plastics.

Member States had to bring into force the national measures necessary to comply with the SUP Directive by 3 July 2021. The Commission is currently assessing the conformity of the legislation adopted by Member States, including by Italy. Depending on the outcome of this assessment, the Commission will decide how to proceed.

Directive (EU) 2019/904 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment, OJ L 155, 12.6.2019, p. 1-19., OJ L 155, 12.6.2019, p. 1-19. Communication — EU policy framework on biobased, biodegradable and compostable plastics of 30 November 2022, COM(2022)682.
